content_voiceover: This is the International Extranodal Lymphoma Study Group prognostic system, the go-to risk score for primary CNS lymphoma, and it's a favorite exam topic. Five adverse factors are counted: age over sixty, ECOG performance status greater than two, elevated LDH, high CSF protein, and tumor location in the deep brain structures like the periventricular region, basal ganglia, brainstem, or cerebellum. Patients are stratified by how many of these five factors they have. With zero risk factors, two year overall survival is excellent, around eighty percent. With one to four factors, it drops substantially to forty-eight percent. And with all five factors present, survival craters to just fifteen percent. The Kaplan-Meier curves from the original Ferreri study, published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology in 2003, show a highly significant separation between these three risk groups, with a p value of 0.00001. This score helps guide prognosis discussions and clinical trial stratification in PCNSL.
keypoints: IELSG score: age >60, PS >2, high LDH, high CSF protein, deep brain lesion
Ferreri et al, JCO 2003; highly significant risk stratification (p=0.00001)
keypoint_voiceover: Know the five IELSG factors: age over sixty, poor performance status, elevated LDH, high CSF protein, and deep brain location. Zero factors gives roughly eighty percent two year survival, one to four factors gives forty-eight percent, and all five factors gives just fifteen percent. This is a classic board question about PCNSL prognosis.
